The '''2018–19 season''' was [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]]'s 27th season in the [[Premier League]] and 41st successive season in the top division of the [[English football league system]]. Along with the [[2018–19 Premier League|league]], the club competed in the [[2018–19 FA Cup|FA Cup]], [[2018–19 EFL Cup|EFL Cup]] and [[2018–19 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]].

The club finished fourth in the Premier League, qualifying for next season's Champions League, and were eliminated by [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]] in the fourth round of the FA Cup. Additionally, they reached the semi-finals of the EFL Cup where they faced [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]]. After two legs the aggregate score was 2–2 and Spurs were eliminated 4–2 on penalties. However, after overcoming [[AFC Ajax|Ajax]] on away goals after two very dramatic legs in the semi-finals, Tottenham reached the [[2019 UEFA Champions League final|Champions League final]] for the first time in the club's history. In an all-English affair, Tottenham lost 0–2 to [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] at the [[Metropolitano Stadium|Wanda Metropolitano]] in [[Madrid]].

Notably, the club made no signings during both the summer and January transfer windows. This was the first time in Premier League history where this has been done.<ref name=SummerWindow>{{cite news |title=Tottenham Hotspur's 2018 summer transfer window, summarized |work=SBNation |last=George-Miller |first=Dustin |date=9 August 2018 |url= https://cartilagefreecaptain.sbnation.com/2018/8/9/17670068/tottenham-hotspur-transfer-news-rumors-spurs-2018-summer-window-summarized |access-date=4 April 2024}}</ref><ref name=JanuaryWindow>{{cite news |title= Tottenham Hotspur January 2019 transfer window summary |work=SBNation |last=George-Miller |first=Dustin |date=31 January 2019 |url= https://cartilagefreecaptain.sbnation.com/2019/1/31/18205974/tottenham-hotspur-transfer-news-rumors-january-window-summary |access-date=4 April 2024}}</ref>

For the majority of the season, the club's matches were played at [[Wembley Stadium]] due to the development of the [[Tottenham Hotspur Stadium]]. On 3 April 2019, the new stadium opened, with the first match being a Premier League game against [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]]. Tottenham won 2–0, with [[Son Heung-min]] scoring the first goal at their new ground.

== Friendlies ==

=== Pre-season ===
Tottenham took part in the [[2018 International Champions Cup]] with scheduled games against [[A.C. Milan]], [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] and [[A.S. Roma|Roma]].<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.espn.com/soccer/international-champions-cup/story/3459323/icc-schedule-features-real-madrid-barcelona-manchester-united-manchester-city-liverpool |title=ICC schedule features Madrid, Barca, Manchester clubs, Liverpool, more |publisher=ESPN|date=17 April 2018 |access-date=7 June 2018}}</ref> After the three games played by all teams taking part Tottenham was declared champions having accumulated seven points and the best goal difference.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.tottenhamhotspur.com/news/2018/august/success-in-icc/ |title=Success in ICC |publisher=Tottenham Hotspur Football Club |date=12 August 2018 |access-date=26 August 2018}}</ref>

==== Fixtures ====
On 14 June 2018, the Premier League fixtures for the forthcoming season were announced.<ref>{{cite news |title=Man City visit Arsenal on first weekend |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44479264 |access-date=14 June 2018 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=14 June 2018}}</ref> Owing to delays in the completion of the club's new stadium, the first fourteen home games of the season were played at Wembley.<ref name="Kilpatrick">{{cite news |url=https://www.standard.co.uk/sport/football/tottenham-confirm-wembley-date-for-manchester-city-match-and-stadium-will-stage-champions-league-a3926521.html |title=Tottenham confirm Wembley date for Manchester City match and stadium will stage Champions League group stage |first=Dan |last=Kilpatrick |work=Evening Standard|date=3 September 2018 |access-date=25 October 2018 }}</ref> Some fixtures were updated after Sky Sports announced their live TV coverage.<ref>{{cite web |title=Fixture changes – August/September |url=https://www.tottenhamhotspur.com/news/2018/july/fixture-changes-augustseptember/ |publisher=Tottenham Hotspur Football Club |access-date=6 July 2018}}</ref>

===FA Cup===
{{main|2018–19 FA Cup}}
Tottenham entered the competition in the third round and were handed an away tie at either [[Tranmere Rovers F.C.|Tranmere Rovers]] or [[Southport F.C.|Southport]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Southport or Tranmere away in the FA Cup|url=https://www.tottenhamhotspur.com/news/2018/december/southport-or-tranmere-in-fa-cup-third-round/|access-date=3 December 2018|work=Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|date=3 December 2018}}</ref> Tranmere Rovers won the replay 2–0, claiming the home draw to play Spurs.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/46435647 |title=Southport 0 - 2 Tranmere Rovers |work=BBC Sport |author=Tom Garry |date=17 December 2018 |access-date=18 December 2018}}</ref>

===EFL Cup===
{{main|2018–19 EFL Cup}}
Due to Wembley Stadium not being available, and Tottenham's new stadium not being complete, the third-round tie against Watford took place at [[Stadium MK]], the home of [[Milton Keynes Dons F.C.|Milton Keynes Dons]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/45434114 |title=Tottenham to host Watford in Carabao Cup at MK Dons |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=6 September 2018 |publisher=BBC Sport |access-date=18 September 2018}}</ref>
